Question Choices: Eight students are divided into labeled teams A and B of sizes 3 and 5. How many different divisions are possible?
Hints: Choose the 3 students for team A;The remaining 5 automatically form team B
Solution: There are $C(8,3)=56$ choices for team A.;Once team A is chosen, team B is determined, so there are $56$ divisions.

Question Choices: Ten students are divided into two labeled teams of size 5. What is the probability that two specified students are on the same team?
Hints: After placing the first student, 9 positions remain;Four positions are on the same team as the first student
Solution: Once the first specified student is placed, $4$ of the remaining $9$ positions are on that student's team.;Thus the probability is $4/9$.

Question Choices: Twelve students are divided into three labeled teams of size 4. What is the probability that three specified students are all on the same team?
Hints: Treat the specified students as occupying 3 of 12 team positions;There are C(12,3) position sets;Each team contributes C(4,3) favorable sets
Solution: There are $C(12,3)=220$ possible position sets.;The three teams contribute $3C(4,3)=12$ favorable sets.;Thus the probability is $12/220=3/55$.
